items.author: Ben (2026-09-10); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: A rolled world cannot be judged, because round 4 never shows whether the arc happened in it
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-10, the second half of the randomise ruling: rolling should give "the player the ability to see if their world will contain these types of structures". Ben placed this IN sprint 38 (elicitation, "in-sprint-38").

RANDOMNESS WITHOUT A READOUT IS NOT A CHOICE. BL-890 makes each arrival a fresh world; this item is what lets the player tell one from another. Without it a reroll is a blind redraw -- the player cannot see whether this world produced an empire, a collapse, or five polities that never fought, so "reroll until it looks interesting" is not actually available to them.

THE STRUCTURES ARE THE ONES GENERATION_STRATEGY.md sec The asymmetry is POLITICAL names: were polities eliminated, did an empire form, did it fall, are the survivors unequal. history_sweep already computes every one of these per world (eliminations, top/peak share, BL-767 rise/peak/fall) -- the quantities exist and are simply not surfaced.

RELATED SURFACES ALREADY DESIGNED: BL-817 (history playback record) and BL-830 (top-sixteen scoreboard) are round 4's instrument. Check what they now cover before adding a surface -- this may be a read on those rather than a new panel. SCOPE THAT FIRST.

DONE WHEN: after round 4 the player can see, without leaving the wizard, whether this world's history contains the arc -- and can reroll on that basis.

=== CAPTURE-VERIFIED 2026-09-11; STILL PARTIAL, AND THE REASON IS NOT COSMETIC. ===

WHAT IS PROVEN. The arc readout renders off today's build and is legible. Headless capture `press_04_round5_history.png` shows, under a "What happened here" rule: "56 polities, 0 destroyed. / The largest empire held 8% of the world; 2 rose and fell back. / At the end the greatest holds 8%, the least 1 region." That is exactly the structure GENERATION_STRATEGY.md sec The asymmetry is POLITICAL names -- eliminations, whether an empire formed, whether it fell, how unequal the survivors are -- in a form a player can read without watching the replay. The item's SUBSTANCE is delivered.

WHAT IS NOT PROVEN, AND IT IS THE HALF THIS ITEM IS ABOUT. The player must be able to REACH the round and reroll on what they see. `history_lapse_press.lua` walks the wizard with real presses and went RED here: four assertions fail, every Next after round 3 misses, and the wizard never leaves round 3 (0-based 2). A purpose-written probe (`scripts/verify/round4_arc_reach.lua`) pressed the column at y = 995, 1005, 1017, 1027, 1040, 1055 and 1070 and NONE advanced the round.

THE LIKELY CAUSE, STATED AS A HYPOTHESIS RATHER THAN A FINDING. Round 3 carries a preference block (Drawdown) that the pass rounds do not, and this item then added three more lines above the footer. The footer follows the column's content, so the Next control appears to sit at or below the bottom edge at this window size -- a surface that grew until it pushed its own exit off the screen. The capture shows a blue footer bar clipped at the very bottom of the panel.

TWO REASONS THIS IS NOT YET CALLED A REGRESSION. (1) The verify window reports "window 1720x1080" while the capture is 1920x1080, so capture pixels and click coordinates may not be the same space, and the probe's misses could be a coordinate-space error rather than an unreachable control. (2) The wizard's left column has a scrollbar, so a human may simply scroll to the footer -- and the verify API has NO scroll verb for that column (`scroll_panel` knows only named ledger windows), so a script cannot test the human path.

WHY IT WAS NOT LIVE-CLICKED. Ben was using the PC (2026-09-11) and asked for captures instead. Worth recording: computer-use resolved "ProjectIo" to `.claude/worktrees/elated-mclean-7dd61c/build/ProjectIo.exe`, a TWO-DAY-OLD binary, while the real build sat at `build/ProjectIo.exe` -- so a live check taken without checking that path would have verified the wrong exe and looked fine doing it.

WHAT REMAINS: establish whether round 3's Next is reachable by a human at 1080p. If it is not, that is a blocker on the whole wizard and not merely on this readout. BL-904 owns the reachability question and the missing scroll verb.
items.resolution:
CODE LANDED 2026-09-11 (fcf118e2). LIVE CHECK OWED -- hence partial, per the standing rule that a UI requirement needs a click and not only a clean compile.

A PURE READ over era_timelapse's existing polity samples. No new field, nothing on the save seam -- which is what the item asked to be checked first, and the answer was that the record already carries everything: population, regions held and capacities per polity per recorded step.

WHAT IT ANSWERS, and it is a different question from the scoreboard beside it. The scoreboard shows who leads RIGHT NOW and re-ranks as the centuries pass. This says whether anything HAPPENED: how many polities, how many were destroyed, the largest empire ever formed, how many rose and fell back, and how unequal the survivors are. That is the question a player rolling a world actually asks, and without it BL-890's reroll is a blind redraw.

EVERY DEFINITION IS history_sweep's OWN, deliberately -- ROSE is a peak at least double the start and at least three regions more, FELL is ending at or under 60% of that peak -- so the panel and the harness cannot drift into describing the same world differently.

A QUIET AGE GETS ITS OWN SENTENCE rather than a row of zeroes, because Ben ruled on 2026-09-10 that a seed refusing war is a legitimate outcome, and a readout that renders it as failure would contradict that.

OWED: open the built app, reach round 4, confirm the panel renders and reads correctly against a world whose arc is known from the sweep.

items.author: Claude (found building BL-899); Ben to confirm priority
items.title: A culture that crossed water to get where it is cannot be told from one that walked
items.design:
FOUND WHILE BUILDING BL-899 (seafaring creed), 2026-09-11. Ben settled that sea legs are earned from THREE upstream facts: a coastal cradle, A CROSSING IN ITS MIGRATION, and a sea or storm god in the pantheon. Only two of the three survive into `creed_state`, so BL-899 shipped deriving `culture::sea_legs_q` from those two and documented the gap at the field.

WHAT IS MISSING, EXACTLY. `colonisation.cpp`'s crude overseas hop KNOWS it coined a daughter on the far side of water -- the fact exists at the moment of spawning. But `culture_spawn` carries only (culture, parent, tile, farm class, year), so nothing reaching `culture` can distinguish a daughter that hopped from one that walked. The fact is produced and then dropped one struct short of its consumer.

THE REPAIR IS SMALL: a `crossed_water` flag on `culture_spawn`, set where the overseas hop already branches, read in `build_creeds` beside the coastal-cradle and sea-god terms that BL-899 already sums.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING RATHER THAN LEAVING. COLONISATION.md sec Culture arrives by route makes the distribution of pantheons A RECORD OF ROUTES, and a water crossing is the single most consequential thing that can happen to a route. It is also the fact with the best claim of the three to EARN sea legs -- a coastal cradle only says where a people started, a sea god says what they believe, but a crossing says what they actually did. Today the one fact that is a deed rather than a circumstance is the one that is thrown away.

DONE WHEN: a culture whose ancestors crossed water carries that fact into `creed_state`, `sea_legs_q` reads all three terms, and the sweep shows sea legs distributed differently from the two-term derivation.

items.author: Claude (found building BL-898)
items.title: pass_one_handoff has seven red rows because its synthetic fixture no longer produces a war
items.design:
FOUND WHILE BUILDING BL-898, 2026-09-11, and PRE-EXISTING -- that item touched nothing this harness covers.

WHAT IS RED: C5a, C5g, C5h, C5i, C5k, C4b and C6b. The cause is one fact, not seven: the harness strip fixture now produces 2 battles, 2 conquests and ZERO GRUDGE PAIRS, so every row that needs a quarrel to exist has nothing to assert against.

THIS IS A FIXTURE FAILURE, NOT A CODE FAILURE, and the distinction is the whole item. The strip was authored when the sim fought readily on it; the sim has since been reshaped repeatedly -- BL-894 made Settle re-settlement, BL-837 gated reach, BL-896 made ground secede -- and the strip stopped being a world where war happens. The rows are correct and the world under them is wrong.

THE TEMPTING FIX IS THE WRONG ONE. Tuning the strip until a war appears is fitting a fixture to its assertions, and the next sim change breaks it again. The BL-898 agent declined to do it and wrote its own G7 against `era_minus_one_fixture` -- the era generation ACTUALLY RUNS -- instead. That is the pattern worth generalising here.

DONE WHEN: the seven rows either assert against a fixture that genuinely produces a war for a reason that will survive the next sim change, or are re-pointed at the real generated era the way BL-898's G7 is, or are retired with the reason recorded. A harness whose red is permanent and explained is worse than one that is either green or deleted -- it trains everyone to ignore it.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-08, as lever 3 of BL-823); Claude (split out on closing that umbrella)
items.title: A polity can act on ground it cannot hear from, because there is no communication rung
items.design:
SPLIT OUT OF BL-823 (anti-hegemon levers) ON 2026-09-11, when that umbrella closed. It is the LAST of its six levers still unbuilt; the other five shipped under their own ids.

BEN, 2026-09-08, naming it: before a communication rung is reached, a polity cannot act on ground it cannot HEAR from -- which bounds early growth by GEOGRAPHY rather than by a cap.

IT EARNS ITS PLACE TWICE, which is why it survived the umbrella's closure. It is an anti-hegemon lever, and it is also THE SECOND RUNG OF BEN'S OWN ARC (GENERATION_STRATEGY.md: origin -> COMMUNICATION -> conquest or diplomatic union -> a stable dark age). The arc names four rungs and this is the only one with no mechanism behind it.

IT IS NOT A DUPLICATE OF REACH, AND THAT DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE ITEM. BL-837's reach asks CAN I SUPPLY THIS -- a question about materials moving over terrain. Communication asks CAN I KNOW ABOUT THIS AT ALL -- a question about information, which travels differently, degrades differently, and binds EARLY history where reach binds late. If the build cannot articulate a difference that shows up in the numbers, it is duplicating reach and should be dropped rather than shipped: BL-823's own instruction was to re-read the remaining levers as SUPPORTING reach-gating and to drop any that only duplicate it. That test applies to this item first.

THE CONSTRAINT, unchanged from the umbrella: a lever is a FORCE WITH A VISIBLE CAUSE ON THE MAP, never a term inside an actor and never a penalty that scales with a polity's rank.

DESIGN IS OWED BEFORE BUILD. Open: what the rung IS (a capacity band? a work? a property of the network?); whether it gates the scorer's candidate list or the verb's execution; and how it differs measurably from reach rather than only in prose.

DONE WHEN: a polity demonstrably cannot act on ground it has no communication to; the bound shows up in EARLY history where reach binds late; and the difference from reach is visible in the sweep rather than argued for in a comment.

items.author: Claude (found capture-verifying BL-891)
items.title: The wizard's scripted walk cannot get past round 3, and no script can test whether a human can
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-11 while capture-verifying BL-891 (round 4 arc readout).

THE SYMPTOM. `history_lapse_press.lua` -- the acceptance script that walks the pre-game wizard with REAL presses through ImGui's hit-test -- has four red rows on main. Every Next press after round 3 misses and the wizard stays on round 3 (0-based 2). A purpose-written probe, `scripts/verify/round4_arc_reach.lua`, pressed the column at seven heights from y=995 to y=1070 and none advanced the round.

THE HYPOTHESIS. Round 3 carries a preference block (Drawdown) the pass rounds do not, and BL-891 then added three lines of arc readout above the footer. The footer follows the column's content, so Next appears to have been pushed to or past the bottom edge at 1080p. The capture shows a footer bar clipped at the panel's bottom. A surface that grew until it pushed its own exit off the screen.

TWO THINGS MUST BE SETTLED, AND THE SECOND IS THE MORE IMPORTANT:

1. IS IT ACTUALLY UNREACHABLE FOR A HUMAN? The left column has a scrollbar, so a person may simply scroll down to the footer. If so this is a scripted-walk problem and a minor layout smell. If NOT, the wizard is BLOCKED at round 3 at 1080p and nothing downstream of it can be reached at all -- which would be a release blocker, not a polish item. Needs a live click; Ben was on the PC when this was found.

2. THE VERIFY API CANNOT ASK THE QUESTION. `verify.scroll_panel` resolves only NAMED ledger windows ("tile", "balance", "corporation", "construction", "acquisitions", "generation_ledger") and knows nothing about the wizard's left column. So no script can reach a control that has fallen below that column's fold, and no script can prove one is reachable. That is a hole in the instrument, and it is why this was found by eye rather than by the harness that exists to find it.

ALSO WORTH A LOOK: the verify run reports "window 1720x1080" while captures are 1920x1080. If capture pixels and click coordinates are not the same space, then every coordinate in every wizard press script was read off a capture in the WRONG space, and the ones that pass do so by luck. That would explain why coordinates "read off captures" keep going stale.

DONE WHEN: round 3's Next is reachable and proven so by a script rather than by eye; `verify` can scroll the wizard column; and the capture-versus-click coordinate space is either confirmed identical or documented as not.

items.author: Claude (converged on independently by three agents in the sprint 38 batch)
items.title: BL-837's reach gate -- the phase's primary lever -- refuses zero campaigns in generation's own run
items.design:
FOUND THREE TIMES INDEPENDENTLY ON 2026-09-11, by three agents working different items who had no contact with each other. That convergence is why this is filed at priority A rather than as an observation.

THE READING, STRAIGHT OFF THE SWEEP: `REFUSED reach gate   median 0   (BL-837)`. Across 16 seeds at --epoch 0, in generation's own run, the reach gate refuses NO campaigns at all.

WHY THAT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. BL-823's own resolution note promoted reach-gating from one lever among six to THE PRIMARY LEVER: "an empire persists while its network holds and fragments when it does not, and the number of nations at 1200 CE is a consequence of what got built and stayed maintainable." CIVILISATION.md sec The road is the empire's skeleton is built on the same claim. If the gate refuses nothing, the primary lever is not doing the job the design assigns it -- whatever else is holding the world multipolar, it is not this.

WHAT IT ALREADY BLOCKED, and each was a real cost paid before the cause was known:
  - BL-887 (reach as centre chains) built a correct, cheap centre-relay model and measured NO movement. Tripling the rebate reproduced the default figures EXACTLY. The agent's diagnosis: cheaper reach can only unlock ground a price was keeping shut, and no ground is shut.
  - BL-839 (turbulence lean) leans three forces and two of them are inert. Its reach-cost term is "a toll on a road nobody is stopped on", and its fear term leans a median of 0 candidates. The lean measured as a null result at calm-vs-turbulent on every headline figure.
  - BL-838 (fear of being next) fires in only 6 of 16 worlds and moved hegemony not at all.

SO THE QUESTION IS NOT "TUNE THE GATE". It is WHY nothing reaches it. Candidates worth measuring before changing anything:
  (a) the water-gate legality test (BL-778) refuses a median 969 wet contacts per world and may simply be consuming every candidate the reach gate would otherwise see -- the two gates are in sequence and the first one may be doing all the work;
  (b) the floors are sited where nothing lands, and the recalibration history (250 -> 80 -> 20 on a related floor) suggests this was suspected before;
  (c) the span. The phase runs 400 of its designed 1,600 years, so realms may never get large enough to outrun their own reach.

DO NOT FIX BY RAISING A FLOOR UNTIL THE CAUSE IS KNOWN. Three wrong diagnoses were published in this file's history and every one was caught by one number contradicting another on the same page. The instrument was right every time; the reasoning ahead of it was not.

DONE WHEN: the reason the reach gate refuses nothing is MEASURED and named; and either the gate refuses a non-trivial share of campaigns, or CIVILISATION.md stops calling it the primary lever and says what actually holds the world multipolar.
